question: The Law of Conservation of Mass was given by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Antoine Lavoisier**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antoine Lavoisier**, a French chemist, is credited with formulating the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, which states that **mass cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction**.
 
• The law was established in the late **18th century**, around **1789**, when Lavoisier demonstrated through meticulous experiments that the total mass of reactants is equal to the total mass of products in a closed system.
 
• Lavoisier is regarded as the "Father of Modern Chemistry" for his contributions to the field, including standardizing chemical nomenclature and identifying elements like oxygen and hydrogen.
 
• The Law of Conservation of Mass laid the foundation for the development of stoichiometry, which allows chemists to calculate quantities of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• This fundamental principle is applied universally in fields like **chemistry, physics, and engineering**, ensuring mass balance in processes ranging from industrial manufacturing to environmental science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Joseph Proust:**

 
 
• Proust is known for the **Law of Definite Proportions**, which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratios by mass.
 
• His work was significant in proving the consistency of chemical compositions in compounds.
 
 
 
• **John Dalton:**
 
 
• Dalton proposed the **Atomic Theory**, which includes the idea that matter is composed of indivisible atoms.
 
• He also formulated the **Law of Multiple Proportions**, which complements the Law of Conservation of Mass.
 
 
 
• **Ernest Rutherford:**
 
 
• Known for discovering the structure of the atom through the **Gold Foil Experiment**, Rutherford identified the nucleus as the central part of the atom.
 
• His work primarily contributed to atomic physics rather than chemical laws like conservation of mass.
 
 
 
• **Key Applications of the Law:**
 
 
• **Industrial Processes:** Used in designing chemical reactors and ensuring material balance in industries like pharmaceuticals and petrochemicals.
 
• **Environmental Science:** Applied in tracking pollutants and ensuring mass conservation in ecological systems.
 
• **Physics:** The principle aligns with the conservation laws of energy and matter in closed systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:**

 
 
• It is a cornerstone of modern chemistry and is essential for understanding chemical reactions and equations.
 
• The law ensures that mass is conserved in any physical or chemical process, highlighting the closed-system nature of reactions.
 
 
 
• **Lavoisier’s Contributions:**
 
 
• Lavoisier also identified and named **oxygen**, recognizing its role in combustion and respiration.
 
• He helped establish a systematic approach to chemical analysis and classification.
 
 
 
• **Experimental Evidence:**
 
 
• Lavoisier meticulously measured the mass of reactants and products using sealed containers to demonstrate conservation principles.
 
• His experiments paved the way for the quantitative study of chemistry.
